meta.ownerNote: This is the only file the map page reads. It is read at build time by src/pages/wardogs-map.mjs and also served as-is at /assets/data/wardogs-map-points.json. Add a location by copying the shape of `template` into `points`. Never guess: if a position has not been read, leave x and y as null and the page will print the row as 'position not read yet' instead of plotting it.
meta.fieldNote: x and y are kilometres. x counts east from the west edge, y counts south from the north edge, so both run 0-16 on every map. gridRef is the lettered 1 km cell: columns A-P west to east, rows 1-16 north to south.

towersCrossCheck.rule: A tower position is written into points only where at least two projects agree. Anything with a single source, and anything where two projects disagree, is listed below instead of being written into points.
towersCrossCheck.caveat: Counting projects is counting publications, not necessarily separate measurements. Three of the four agree to within 23 metres, which is tighter than separate surveys of the same ground usually land, so several of them are probably working from one upstream calibration - most likely the game's own files. None of the four says so, and this file cannot prove it either way. Treat the source count as the number of places the position is written down, not as four witnesses.
towersCrossCheck.how: Every project's position was converted to this file's kilometres: fraction of the map x 16 km, x counted from the west edge and y from the north edge. apollyon-sys/wardogs-calculator stores game coordinates with y running north (its js/map/map-view.js worldToLocalScreen reads y as bounds.maxY - y), so its y was flipped first. The community projects treat the map they draw as 16 km across; the calculator's own tiles are 16384 px, which it also labels 16.384 km, so a position can sit about 0.2 km further out on a 1:1 reading - see notYetRecorded.
